comment: backdrop-filter at the viewport's edges (fork P7-F2 leaves it as it was): glass panes half beyond each edge and one inside, over stripes across the cut edge. Chromium reads the viewport's backdrop and mirrors it at the viewport's edge, as the engine does (the pane's border box within the viewport, mirrored at its edges): the panes match there and along their other edges, except one 80 x 4 px band along the top edge of the pane cut by the viewport's bottom edge, where Chromium's blur takes about 17 % of the rows above the pane (a sampling detail of its backdrop at an element cut by the viewport; the pane cut by the top edge, over the same stripes, is mirrored like the engine's). Measured 0.407 %, one cluster of 318 px (that band), the same before and after P7-F2, and the same on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (Vulkan, driver 580). Limits: that plus ~30 % (0.53 %, cluster 413 px) for other GPUs.
